articles.title: The clinical day and staff schedule

review.reviewStatus: Draft summary from the 2026 NICU Staff Playbook; QGenda is the source of truth for the schedule

blocks.text: Source: NICU Staff Playbook 2026, sections 3-4. Draft summary for orientation; confirm current expectations with NICU leadership.

The clinical day (Main Campus). Early daytime staff arrive at 6:30 AM for sign-out in the NICU conference room per the long/short call delineation; night staff arrive at 6:30 PM. Structured handoffs support early planning for extubations and step-down transfers.

8:30 AM Dispo rounds - multidisciplinary rounds in G20 with Assistant Nurse Managers, case management, neurosurgery, and stroke to discuss dispositions, expedite transfers, and prepare planned admissions.
9:00 AM Bedside team rounds - systems-based and nurse-led; the responsible resident, fellow, and LIP add assessment and plan. Bedside teaching encouraged; aim to finish by noon.
ICU checklist - completed verbally and in Epic at the end of rounds for every patient.
1:00 PM Line/device huddle - review indwelling devices and ongoing necessity with ANMs and the team.
A long call / short call model may be used, with short call leaving at 4:30 PM and the remaining staff member cross-covering both ICUs and consults.
Staff schedule. The goal is fair, equitable distribution of clinical coverage. QGenda is the official schedule and only up-to-date source of truth; spreadsheets are for viewing only.
Shift definitions: Weekday AM (Mon-Fri), Weekend AM (Sat-Sun), Weekday PM (Mon-Wed), Weekend PM (Thu-Sun). Rest days are post-call days fully exempt from clinical and administrative duties.
Full-time NCC clinical commitment is 28 five-day weeks; partial FTE is proportioned. Scheduling is done in 6-month blocks (Jan-Jun, Jul-Dec) released at least 3 months in advance.
Recovery: one recovery day (Monday) after a weekend shift; two recovery days (Monday and Tuesday) after a 7-day shift.

Night (PM) rotation: full-FTE CV Center providers complete two 6-week night rotations per year (2 weeks and 2 weekends each); adjusted for shared FTE; opt-out available after age 55 in exchange for extra weekend shifts.
Holidays are distributed equally on a rotating basis (mid-year: Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day; end-of-year: Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day).
Time away.

Off-service requests: up to two full weeks per semester, emailed to the unit director and schedule lead strictly before September 1 (Jan-Jun) and March 1 (Jul-Dec). Holiday weeks and popular meeting weeks (NCS, SCCM, AAN) are excluded.

Vacation: requested only after the schedule is released, during non-clinical days; a call switch must be arranged first if during a clinical week. Maximum contiguous vacation is 10 weekdays (14 days total); longer needs CV Center Director approval. 90 days' notice required.
Each provider has one well-being day and one floating holiday, requestable any time that does not interfere with clinical duties.
Meetings: NI funds one meeting per year; rank top 3 for the next calendar year by September 1. Officers, committee members, and presenters get priority for their meeting.

Post-release changes: providers arrange their own call switches (except emergencies); changes are tracked but not counted toward FTE. Emergencies are escalated by phone/email to the unit director and schedule lead. The coordinator updates QGenda.

blocks.text: Source: 2026 Adult Inpatient Bleeding CVAD from Insertion to Maintenance Algorithm (Best Practice; Monica Cummins, MSN, APRN, ACCNS-AG, PCCN, Clinical Nurse Specialist; algorithm March 2026). Draft summary; follow product manufacturer instructions for use (MIFU) and the CLABSI resource site.

A standardized approach to bleeding central venous access devices (CVAD) reduces variation, misused products, and CLABSI risk from frequent dressing changes, and improves cross-discipline collaboration.
Manual pressure is first, prior to any products.
Insertion: the procedure is not complete if the patient requires a pressure dressing for hemostasis or if bleeding persists.
Maintenance: apply products only as indicated and escalate for assistance if needed.
Use only products consistent with MIFU. Do NOT use Surgicel on CVADs. Document products and interventions in the EHR.

Complex/coagulopathic bleeding: QuikClot topical hemostatic 3.8 cm x 3.8 cm pre-slit (manufacturer number 188) may be used; do not put the slit under the catheter - place it on top to absorb bleeding.
Reference: Adult Inpatient CVAD Dressing Troubleshooting Guide and the CLABSI Line Maintenance and Handling resource. Share with nursing, IP, physicians/LIPs, and SQPE.

review.reviewStatus: Draft summary of the enterprise MDSR Playbook (HAI Governance v1.0, 01.30.2026); follow the current playbook and REDCap tools

blocks.text: Source: Standardized Multidisciplinary Device Surveillance Rounding (MDSR) Playbook (HAI Governance, Version 1.0, 01.30.2026). Draft summary; follow the current playbook and REDCap tools on the Infection Prevention Landing Page.

MDSR is a required, standardized, multidisciplinary rounding process for central lines and indwelling urinary catheters across Cleveland Clinic hospitals. Rounds occur at least weekly to confirm insertion and maintenance bundle compliance, evaluate necessity, consider alternatives, and reduce CAUTI and CLABSI. MDSR replaces prior collaborative rounds.
Team: provider/LIP (physician or APP), nursing leadership/quality, Clinical Nurse Specialists, Infection Preventionists, and Nursing Quality representatives.

Central line assessment includes labeled/current tubing, blood-free connectors and lumens, correctly placed CHG/Algidex disc, clean/dry/dated dressing that is not overdue, a clear insertion site, and Curos caps where appropriate.
Urinary catheter assessment includes documented peri/catheter care, intact seal and securement, no dependent loops, bag below bladder level and off the floor, and a bag that is not overfilled.
LIP review covers insertion checklist use, indication, line type/location, Foley order and Nurse Driven Foley Removal (NDFR) order, duration, and keep/remove/replace decisions.
Number of devices to review weekly (by inpatient device volume):

Data (CLA, UCA, and MDSR summaries) is entered in REDCap the day rounds are completed for enterprise tracking. If an opportunity is found in more than 10% of rounds (goal 90% or higher compliance), implement targeted insertion, maintenance, or necessity interventions.

Removal considerations: remove central lines not used for more than 24 hours for central-access meds (48 hours for dialysis/apheresis), avoid lines for lab draws only, and remove urinary catheters when the original need is gone (external catheters can often measure output; consider bladder scans).

articles.title: Urinary retention in the acute care setting

review.reviewStatus: Draft summary of an enterprise LIP guidance document (final 5-13-2026); not a clinical protocol approval

blocks.text: Source: Urinary retention in the acute care setting / acute illness (physician/LIP guidance, final 5-13-2026). Draft summary for orientation; this is not a clinical protocol approval. Confirm current guidance and consult urology as indicated.

Acute urinary retention is the sudden inability to voluntarily pass urine (possibly with suprapubic pain, bloating, or urgency). Chronic retention is a post-void residual (PVR) greater than 300 mL persisting at least 6 months on two separate occasions.
Initial assessment considerations.
Evaluate precipitating medications (anticholinergics, alpha-adrenergic agonists, calcium channel blockers, opioids, benzodiazepines, muscle relaxants) and consider holding contributors.

Assess comorbidities (BPH, spinal cord injury, fecal impaction, chronic constipation, diabetic neuropathy, neurologic illness, deconditioning), perform a focused exam, and review labs (glucose, HgbA1c, urinalysis with reflex culture) and imaging.
Consider a urology consult to facilitate the plan of care.
Determine etiology: obstructive, infectious, post-operative, or neurologic/medical.

Neurologic/medical: intermittent catheterization (IC) is first-line; evaluate glucose/HgbA1c for neurogenic bladder; bladder scan to monitor PVR. If IC volume is under 500 mL, next IC in 6 hours; if not, next IC in 4 hours.

Obstructive (BPH, fecal impaction/constipation, urethral stricture, or post-operative): treat the cause; for BPH start/resume an alpha-blocker at insertion and maintain the indwelling catheter at least 3 days before a trial of void (TOV).
Infectious: obtain diagnostic imaging and urinalysis with reflex culture; consider urology consult.
A TOV is successful when the patient voids with PVR 150-400 mL and no retention symptoms; if unsuccessful, resume catheterization and arrange urology follow-up.

Key terms: IUC (indwelling urinary catheter), IC (intermittent catheterization), TOV (trial of void), PVR (post-void residual). Interpret bladder scans cautiously with ascites, obesity, or anasarca, and defer catheter placement to urology for special cases (e.g., artificial urinary sphincter, recent urethroplasty/prostatectomy).

review.reviewStatus: Draft summary of the July 2026 heparin nomogram update; verify current order sets and ranges in Epic

blocks.text: Source: LIP Heparin Nomogram Updates presentation (July 2026; Enterprise Anticoagulation Committee and Pharmacy & Therapeutics). Draft summary; verify current order sets, ranges, and eligibility in Epic. Questions: anticoagstewardship@ccf.org.

Heparin anti-Xa nomograms became available July 7, 2026 as the standard of practice for IV heparin monitoring. Excluded locations: Ohio Region (Ashtabula Regional Medical Center, Union Hospital, and all Freestanding EDs) and Florida Region (Indian River and the Martin Health System).

Rationale: faster time to therapeutic, more consistent levels unaffected by acute-phase reactants, lupus anticoagulant, or factor deficiencies, and fewer lab draws. Standard target is 0.3-0.7 units/mL for most indications.

Limitations: the assay is affected by oral factor Xa inhibitors (apixaban, edoxaban, rivaroxaban), low-molecular-weight heparin, and fondaparinux. Patients exposed to DOACs or parenteral Xa inhibitors within 5 days are monitored by aPTT.

The order set prompts anti-Xa eligibility screening (outpatient factor Xa inhibitor history in the past 180 days; inpatient administrations in the past 5 days) and standardized baseline labs and monitoring; there is no change to nomogram order structure or dosing.

review.reviewStatus: Draft workflow summary; organ donation is coordinated by Lifebanc and requires named clinical review before use

blocks.text: Source: DCD (Donation after Circulatory Determination of Death) Workflow. Draft summary for orientation; organ donation is coordinated by Lifebanc and this page requires named clinical review before operational use. References include the HRSA DCD directives (January 2026) and the AST-ASTS Joint Statement on DCD (2025 Update).
Referral and independence.
Lifebanc is notified prior to DNR-CC withdrawal of life-sustaining support; the primary team confirms the withdrawal decision independent of donation.
Hospital management (before OR).
Confirm withdrawal remains clinically appropriate (reassess q12h and within 2h of withdrawal); obtain and scan legal authorization for DCD into the EMR; consult palliative/hospice if needed.

The primary team maintains medical management until death; Lifebanc does NOT write pre-pronouncement orders. Code status (DNR-CCA vs organ-preservation) and consent for procedures/anticoagulants and NRP use are clarified with the family and Lifebanc.

A multidisciplinary pre-OR huddle (Lifebanc, ICU nurse, staff physician, and the independent accompanying physician who will pronounce) is completed; an arterial line is working (upper-extremity if NRP thoracic recovery), and a reintubation plan and disposition plan (if death does not occur) are established.
Operating room management.

OR huddle confirms code status and comfort measures; the surgical team exits prior to withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy (WLST); heparin is administered per consent; extubation and discontinuation of mechanical/pharmacologic support are performed.

After zero pulse pressure on the arterial line (or absent Doppler flow) and cessation of respiration, a 5-minute observation with continuous zero pulse pressure and strict no-touch conditions is maintained; the period restarts if any cardiac impulse or Doppler activity is detected.

Death is pronounced and documented by the accompanying physician; the organ recovery team enters only AFTER pronouncement. Late autoresuscitation during procurement requires stopping, repeating the 5-minute asystole confirmation with no-touch, and communicating with the OPO and surgical team before restarting.
If death does not occur, the patient is transferred to an appropriate bed and comfort measures continue.

articles.title: Determination of Death by Neurologic Criteria (DNC) in adults

review.reviewStatus: Draft procedure summary; DNC/brain death determination requires MyLearning training and named clinical review before use

blocks.text: Source: DNC flow chart procedure (V2). Draft summary for orientation; determination of death by neurologic criteria (DNC / brain death) requires DNC MyLearning course completion and named clinical review before operational use. References include the World Brain Death Project (JAMA 2020) and the AAN 2023 consensus guideline.
Prerequisites (all must be met).

DNC MyLearning course completed; printed DNC procedure at the bedside. Coma is irreversible and the cause is known, with neuroimaging compatible with the clinical findings (catastrophic supratentorial injury; posterior fossa injury must show a compatible catastrophic picture).

CNS depressant drug effect absent (e.g., pentobarbital serum level under 5 mcg/mL, ethanol under 80 mg/dL; wait 5 or more elimination half-lives when levels cannot be measured); no residual paralytics; no severe acid-base, electrolyte, or endocrine abnormality.

Normothermia (core temperature above 36 C for more than 24 hours); SBP at least 100 mmHg and MAP above 75 mmHg (vasopressors permitted); no spontaneous respirations. Contact Lifebanc and the end-of-life care team as needed.
Clinical examination (Exam 1 and Exam 2; all findings must be present on each exam).
Pupils mid-size to dilated (3 mm or larger), non-reactive to bright light; corneal reflex absent; oculocephalic reflex absent (only if C-spine integrity ensured) and oculovestibular reflex absent.

No facial movement to noxious stimuli at the supraorbital nerve or temporomandibular joint; gag reflex absent; cough reflex absent to tracheal suctioning; no motor response to noxious stimuli in all four limbs (spinally mediated reflexes are permissible).
If the oculocephalic reflex cannot be assessed due to cervical spine or skull-base concerns, DNC can still be determined without ancillary testing if oculovestibular reflexes are absent bilaterally.
Apnea testing and ancillary testing.

Apnea testing follows once prerequisites are met (see the Apnea testing procedure page). A positive test is an arterial pH under 7.30 with PaCO2 of 60 mmHg or higher and at least 20 mmHg above baseline.

Ancillary testing (TCD, cerebral angiogram, or nuclear scintigraphy cerebral blood-flow study) is required when the clinical exam or apnea test cannot be completed or interpreted with certainty, or when confounders cannot be resolved; for ventricular assist devices or aortic balloon pump, consider cerebral angiogram or nuclear scintigraphy. Ancillary testing is not a substitute for a complete clinical brain death examination.

Time of death is the time arterial pH and PaCO2 reached the target value reported in the record; when apnea or the clinical exam cannot be fully performed, it is when the ancillary test is officially reported.

review.reviewStatus: Draft procedure summary; requires DNC training and named clinical review before use

blocks.text: Source: DNC flow chart procedure (V2), apnea testing. Draft summary; requires DNC training and named clinical review before use. Reference: Bein & Citerio, Intensive Care Med 2019 (brain death under extracorporeal life support).
Apnea test in ventilated patients.
Patient is hemodynamically stable (vasopressors may keep SBP above 100 mmHg and MAP above 75) with no major electrolyte, acid-base, or metabolic derangement.
Adjust the ventilator to normocarbia (PaCO2 35-45 mmHg) and pH 7.35-7.45 (unless a CO2 retainer); pre-oxygenate with 100% FiO2 for more than 10 minutes.
Disconnect the ventilator and provide oxygen via extension tubing near the carina at 6 L/min; spontaneous respirations should be absent.

Draw arterial blood gas at 5-7 minutes and every 5 minutes until the goal PaCO2 is reached, then reconnect the ventilator. A positive test is pH under 7.30 with PaCO2 of 60 mmHg or higher and at least 20 mmHg above baseline, with absent respiration.

Abort for SBP under 100 or MAP under 75 despite support, oxygen saturation below 85%, or a cardiac arrhythmia with hemodynamic instability. If normal pH/PaCO2 cannot be maintained, ancillary testing is mandatory in addition to apnea testing.
Apnea test on ECMO.

Coordinate with the primary ICU team. Adjust the ECMO sweep and/or ventilator to physiologic pH and eucapnia (PaCO2 35-45 mmHg); for VA or hybrid ECMO use right upper-extremity arterial and post-oxygenator gases, and for VV ECMO any arterial line is sufficient.

Keep the oxygenator FdO2 at 100%; disconnect the ventilator and oxygenate via a cannula at the carina at 6-9 L/min; gradually reduce the gas sweep to as low as 0.5 L/min as tolerated; watch for any respiratory movement including a brief gasp.

Repeat ABGs after 5-10 minutes and every 5 minutes until the goal PaCO2 is reached while the patient remains stable; the same positive-test threshold and abort criteria apply, reinitiating ECMO on the prior settings if aborted.
